title: Fallback eviction & accelerator rotation playbook (notes)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, pragmatic runbook for graceful node eviction when an accelerator (GPU/TPU-like) needs replacement, and for rotating accelerators with minimal disruption. It is meant as a working playbook for on-call, SRE-led maintenance windows, and emergency recovery when the normal hot-swap path fails.

Scope and when to use:
- Use when a single node or rack reports persistent accelerator errors (ECC, driver crashes, NVLink errors) and immediate replacement is required.
- Also covers emergent capacity add (bring node online), partial accelerator rotation (swap 1/2 accelerators), and fallback routing when pods can’t be scheduled to preferred nodes.
- Not a hardware RMA guide — refer to HW team checklist for physical replacement steps. This focuses on cluster-level safety and preserving customer latency/SLOs.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) Identify impact (pods affected, models, tenant isolation).
2) If node is salvageable, cordon + targeted eviction (drain with grace, skip unsafe pods).
3) If hardware replacement is required immediately, prepare backfill nodes / adjust autoscaler bump.
4) For partial accelerator swap, prefer live rotate with per-pod affinity taints.
5) If scheduling fails, fallback to compatible model variant + route policy.

Initial triage checklist (oncall):
- Alert source: which monitoring fired? (metrics, kernel logs, nvlink alerts, node exporter)
- Confirm node health: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep <node-id>
- Identify affected pods: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep <node-id>
- Check node-level GPU state: 
  - nvidia-smi -q (or equivalent) for errors
  - dmesg | grep -i nvrm / gpu / nvidia
  - system logs for driver OOMs, ECC errors
- Check model routing: which services are pinned to this node (nodeAffinity / preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution)?
- Customer impact: query console for error spikes, latency regressions, or throttles. Notify CS on potential incidents.

Decision gates (quick):
- If transient (single driver crash) -> attempt driver restart + kubelet restart, monitor 10m.
- If recurring hardware ECC / PCIe errors or persistent CUDA failures -> schedule replacement and follow evacuation path.
- If node is under heavy critical-serving load (no capacity elsewhere) -> open incident, activate fallback routing to cheaper/broader model variant.

Eviction procedure (graceful preferred):
1) Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
   - Note: cordon prevents new pods; essential to avoid cascading new-scheduling to a broken node.
2) Annotate node with reason: kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/sre-evict-reason="accel-failure-<short-id>"
3) Identify critical pods (list in priorityClass or have annotations): kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {"priority:"}{.spec.priorityClassName}{"\n"}{end}'
4) Drain non-critical pods first: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --pod-selector='!critical'
   - If drain fails due to PDBs, consult owners: slack #app-owners or send message via incident template.
5) For critical pods that cannot be safely evicted, consider one of:
   - Temporarily mark node as degraded and leave pods running while isolating node-level resources (taint to avoid new pods).
   - If hardware replacement can be done without power-cycle, coordinate with HW to do a live accelerator reseat.
6) After safe eviction of movable pods, monitor cluster for rescheduling progress and capacity pressure.

Partial accelerator rotation (swap one card in place):
- Use only when HW team confirms partial-swap is supported by board (risk: system may require full reboot).
- Flow: cordon node -> taint node with redwood/rotation=in-progress -> schedule canary pods on new backfill node for validation -> pause scheduling on node until hardware validated -> after physical swap, run post-swap validation (nvidia-smi, synthetic microbench perf test, model smoke test).
- If post-swap validation fails, follow full DR path (drain, replace, reprovision).

Emergency hardware replacement (fast path):
- If node must be powered down and physical swap performed:
  1) Ensure critical pods evacuated or have fallback variants.
  2) Add temporary capacity: trigger autoscaler policy to add X nodes (suggested: +20% of current GPU pool) or request on-call infra to spin hot-spare nodes.
  3) Mark node as maintenance in inventory and update incident tracker.
  4) After replacement, rejoin node: run node acceptance test (see acceptance checklist below).

Acceptance checklist (post-replace):
- OS boot clean, kubelet in Ready state, GPU visible: nvidia-smi shows correct device count
- Kernel logs clean for last 5 minutes (no ECC/PCIe errors)
- Run short model-inference smoke test (use staging model) — latency within expected bounds
- Run Kalman-style throughput sanity test for 2 minutes (ensure no throttling)
- Remove maintenance taints/cordon only after tests pass.

Capacity-add and backfill guidance: 
- Preferred approach: bring up dedicated backfill nodes in the same zone, label them with temporary label redwood/backfill=true and set a lower priorityClass so non-critical pods can migrate there.
- For scheduling storms, temporarily allow burst capacity by applying patch to autoscaler: increase max nodes + adjust scale-up delay to 30s for urgent incident.
- If autoscaler is unavailable, manual cloud instance launch (compute team runbook) — keep instance type parity where possible.

Fallback routing and serving considerations: 
- If we cannot restore capacity quickly, use Redwood routing policy: route to compatible smaller quantized model variant or send to Dedicated fallback pool. Ops steps:
  - Update routing config: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/route -d '{"service":"s1","variant":"small-quant"}'
  - Announce to customers (CS templated message).
- Ensure quality monitoring alerts are muted for transient switch so noise is controlled.

Post-incident notes and action items (for retrospective):
- Collect: node logs (journalctl -u kubelet), dmesg, nvidia-smi history, prometheus GPU metrics, scheduling events, and routing changes. Save to incident artifact.
- Run a quick postmortem template: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, owner, ETA on fixes.
- Suggested followups: improve PDBs for critical inference pods, add early-warning metrics for ECC counts, document supported partial-rotation hardware models.

Commands cheat-sheet (copy for on-call):
- Show node: kubectl describe node <node>
- List pods on node: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- Cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- Drain non-critical: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --pod-selector='!critical'
- Uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>
- Annotate: kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/sre-evict-reason="accel-failure-<id>"

Known gotchas / lessons learned (from prior incidents):
- Draining can hang if CSI volume detach is slow — pre-check attach/detach metrics and call storage on slow detach.
- Some models assume GPU UUID stable; avoid doing partial-rotation during peak traffic for those models.
- Autoscaler cooldowns often prevent quick surge; keep an emergency quickscale policy ready.
- Hardware teams sometimes require a full-machine firmware update after swap — plan for that time.

Open TODOs (work items to make this playbook better):
- Add automated script to perform selective drain by priorityClass (owner: Carlos)
- Formalize acceptance test suite for accelerators beyond basic smoke (owner: Priya)
- Hook routing fallback to an automated circuit-breaker tied to GPU error rate (owner: infra-reliability)

Slack and escalation shortcuts:
- Incident channel: #sre-incident (use template: :rotating_light: [EVAC] <node> - <short-reason>)
- Hardware paging: @hw-oncall
- Product/Owners: use /incident notify template to target groups with potential customer impact.

Appendix: brief example incident timeline (fictional)
- 09:02 — monitoring: ECC count spike on node gpu-23 -> alert
- 09:04 — oncall confirms recurring driver reset, cordon node
- 09:10 — non-critical pods drained, critical model pinned; fallback routing enabled to quantized variant
- 09:24 — hardware swap scheduled, autoscaler bumped +2 nodes
- 10:03 — replacement done, acceptance tests pass, node uncordoned at 10:18

Notes to self: keep this short, add links to acceptance scripts and the HW RMA form. This should remain a living doc — prefer clarity over completeness for oncall reading.

End of doc.
